rules.sentence: Synovial sarcomas are treated aggressively with limb-sparing surgery and frequently chemotherapy.

Immunohistochemistry is helpful in identifying these tumors, since the tumor cells, especially in the biphasic type, are positive for epithelial antigens (e.g., keratins), differentiating them from many other sarcomas.
The 5-year survival varies from 25% to 62%, related to stage and patient age.
UPSs are aggressive malignancies that are treated with surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy and/or radiation.
The prognosis is generally poor, with metastases arising in 30% to 50% of cases.
